question: Can a deterministic front-matter/link/index sweeper plus a cheap haiku relevance check usefully flag stale docs?
notes: 5 of 7 docs have no front-matter, so they report errors and status 'unknown' and are never sent to the LLM.
With --today 2027-03-01 only the 2 front-mattered docs are stale candidates; both go to haiku.
Haiku keep on spike-phase plan reasoned from the real date (created today) rather than the forced 150d age: plausible, but shows the model cannot be told a fake today reliably.
Haiku refine on the design spec cites 'spike execution status unclear' - plausible, human review recommended.
~85 s per call on a loaded machine (full claude startup + ~60-file listing in prompt); a sweep of 8 docs costs ~10+ minutes.
claude missing verified by removing it from PATH: verdict 'unavailable', run completes, exit code unaffected.
howToRun: dotnet run sweep.cs -- ../../../docs [--today 2027-03-01] [--json] [--llm]; dotnet run sweep.cs -- --selftest
